input.rationale: Investigate a sourced same-operation context mismatch in batched quorum-confirmed ReadIndex replies. Construct an actual bootstrap/election/read prefix and compare raw request and returned contexts with origin-based identity before making any defect conclusion.

investigations.question: When one follower read is still pending and a later read from another follower obtains a quorum confirmation, does the leader return each original request context to the correct origin?
investigations.hypothesis: readIndex.confirm returns and removes a prefix of readStatus objects, preserving each original ctx and from. handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation uses s.from and s.index but m.Hint/m.HintHigh on remote replies, apparently replacing earlier contexts with the latest confirmation context. The follower exposes that context in ReadyToRead, and pendingReadIndex.addReady only recognizes its own batches by exact SystemCtx.
investigations.discriminator: Launch three real Peers from empty TestLogDB stores and bootstrap addresses; elect normally with logical ticks and commit the current-term no-op. Submit one unique context from each follower. Compare normal first-round delivery with loss of only the first request heartbeat round, followed by reliable delivery for the second request and twelve heartbeat rounds. Identify each operation by scenario and origin, never returned context. Inspect producer messages, pending statuses, consumer ReadyToReads and missing outcomes. A preserved original context or an enclosing rule preventing overlapping remote requests would refute the suspicion.
counterevidence: The local-leader completion branch uses s.ctx correctly.
The first read cannot be served before a current-term entry commits in a multi-voter cluster.
Nonzero-context heartbeat broadcasts target voting members, not observers.
Existing TestReadOnlyOptionSafe checks returned context equality for serial reads; it does not establish overlapping-request behavior.
limitations: No retained execution has been reviewed yet.
The proposed endpoint is the Peer ReadyToRead interface. Client RequestState timeout, FSM read contents and any linearizability consequence are not measured.

scope.description: Three normal bootstrapped voting Peers in one synchronously owned memory transport. Compare the same two follower ReadIndex inputs under two delivery schedules. The only fault is losing the two initial context-bearing heartbeat messages in the treatment; later communication is reliable.
assumptions: No crashes, membership changes or persistence failures. The existing TestLogDB models successful storage; updates are appended and state saved before messages are delivered.

The harness applies actual committed bootstrap configuration entries and acknowledges committed indices through Peer.NotifyRaftLastApplied. There is no application command/FSM read in this local interface probe.

Each follower submits exactly one distinct, nonzero opaque SystemCtx via the real Peer.ReadIndex producer. Contexts are supplied instead of executing the node-level random generator; Peer.ReadIndex and the existing context-equality test independently establish that this argument must be preserved.
Logical time is controlled. Node 1 alone ticks until election; after requests, all three nodes receive twelve ticks with each message queue fully drained.
excluded: Public NodeHost futures and timeout completion
Any universal progress guarantee inferred from twelve ticks

experiment.prefix: For each independent scenario, Launch all three peers with empty TestLogDB and the same three bootstrap addresses. Save each update; apply actual committed configurations and notify applied indices. Tick node 1 until its election and current-term no-op are committed, routing every real message. Submit context (1001,31) at follower 2; either deliver its complete round or discard only generated Heartbeat messages. Submit context (2002,32) at follower 3 and deliver all traffic. Then tick and deliver twelve normal rounds. The test never injects term, leader, commit, pending-read, membership or reply state. Every returned ReadyToRead is emitted with origin identity regardless of context; endpoint counts retain missing or duplicate results.
experiment.requirement: A ReadIndex result returned at the originating Peer must preserve both fields of the SystemCtx supplied for that read. Batched confirmation may raise the read index, but cannot substitute a different operation context.
experiment.responsibility: Peer.ReadIndex takes SystemCtx and forwards its two fields; TestReadOnlyOptionSafe explicitly expects returned ReadyToRead.SystemCtx to equal the request context. node.handleReadIndex registers that same context before calling the Peer, and pendingReadIndex.addReady uses exact SystemCtx to associate readiness with the pending batch. Therefore context preservation is an independently applicable local interface responsibility, without claiming every admitted read must always succeed or that this probe measures a client timeout.

comparisons.description: Compare the observed low context word with the input for the sole request at that origin, independent of output context.
Compare the observed high context word with the input for the sole request at that origin.

result.summary: Prepared a sourced ReadIndex context-preservation probe with normal bootstrap, election, and a delivery control. Draft validation passed; controller execution and evidence review remain pending.
